analysis.title: SAIA (SAIA) 3Q26 EPS Beat on Revenue and Margins; Remain Buy Rated on Freight Recovery
key_insights: SAIA (Buy) reported 3Q26 recurring EPS of $3.41 versus FactSet consensus of $3.30 and GSe of $3.28. Revenue of $982mn was +1.5% above consensus and +1.3% above GSe.

The adjusted operating ratio was 87.6%, 20bps better than the 87.8% consensus and 30bps better than the 87.9% GSe. Higher revenue plus slightly better margins put adjusted EBIT about 3-4% above forecasts ($122mn vs $118mn).

Salaries expense was the largest positive variance against GS forecasts (45.6% of revenue vs 46.3% GSe). Purchased transportation (9.2% vs 8.9%) and fuel and operating expenses (21.7% vs 21.5%) partly offset it.
Tonnage per day grew +8.9% YoY versus +8.4% in 2Q26 and -2.1% in 1Q26, helped by an easier compare (3Q25 tonnage was -1.5% YoY). GSe was about +8.5%.
Revenue per hundredweight including fuel surcharge grew +7.4% YoY versus the +6.9% GS estimate. Ex-fuel yield was -2.2% YoY versus -3.0% GSe, as weight per shipment rose +8.1% (mix efforts).

Management said October tons per day were up about 10% YoY, in line with September at +10.3%. That compares with 4Q consensus of about +8.6% and GSe of +8.0% before the print. GS now forecasts 4Q26 tonnage at +9.0% YoY because Nov/Dec comps are tougher.

Management guided the 3Q to 4Q margin deterioration to about 200bps, better than the historical seasonal 250-300bps. That implies a 4Q OR near 87.6%. Consensus before the print was 89.7% and GS was 90.1%. GS's new 4Q OR estimate is 89.6%.

Ex-fuel yield rose 1.5% QoQ despite the heavier weight per shipment. New terminals' revenue per shipment ex-fuel improved faster YoY than legacy terminals. Recent contract renewals were up 10.8%. GS expects ex-fuel yield growth to stay negative near term as the freight mix gets heavier.

GS raised FY26/27/28 EPS to $11.43/$14.35/$17.10 from $11.15/$14.25/$17.00 on the 3Q beat and higher revenue and margin trajectory. It projects about 25% and 19% YoY EPS growth in 2027 and 2028, with incremental margins of about 30%.

The 12-month price target stays at $472 (45.4% upside from $324.62). The target P/E multiple was lowered to about 28.5x from about 30x, consistent with the ODFL cut and within a 10-15% discount to the applied ODFL multiple. It is applied to Q5-Q8 EPS of $16.54.

GS keeps a Buy on SAIA on the potential manufacturing recovery. It argues the LTL sector's operating leverage and incremental margins should give it some of the strongest transport upside over the medium term. A Blue Sky case, with a firmer freight recovery lifting yields and incrementals, would give sharper upside at existing P/E multiples.

market_movers.rationale: Buy reiterated after a 3Q26 beat on revenue and margins, with EPS estimates raised and the price target unchanged at $472. The target P/E multiple was lowered to about 28.5x from about 30x.

sector_views.rationale: GS says the LTL sector should show some of the strongest transport upside over the medium term. Operating leverage and incremental margins would benefit from higher density as manufacturing volumes recover.

earnings_insights: SAIA 3Q26 recurring EPS reported $3.41 vs FactSet consensus est $3.30 and GSe $3.28 (beat of 3.3% vs consensus, 4.0% vs GSe). Recurring net income reported $91mn vs GSe $88mn and consensus $89mn.
SAIA 3Q26 revenue reported $982mn vs consensus est $968mn (+1.5%) and GSe $970mn (+1.3%). Adjusted EBIT reported $122mn vs consensus est $118mn (+3.3%) and GSe $118mn (+3.8%).
SAIA 3Q26 adjusted operating ratio reported 87.6% vs consensus est 87.8% and GSe 87.9%. LTL revenue ex-fuel reported $731.9mn, +6.6% YoY, vs GSe $722.8mn (+5.2% YoY).

SAIA guided 3Q to 4Q margin deterioration to about 200bps versus the historical 250-300bps. The implied 4Q OR is about 87.6% versus pre-print consensus est 89.7% and GSe 90.1%. GS's new 4Q OR estimate is 89.6%.
GS FY26E/27E/28E EPS estimates (GSe) are $11.43/$14.35/$17.10, up from $11.15/$14.25/$17.00. GS's 4Q26E EPS is $2.65 (GSe).
SAIA total shipments reported 2,351K (+0.8% YoY) vs GSe 2,356K (+1.0% YoY). Total LTL tons reported 1,722K, +8.9% YoY vs GSe +8.5%.
risk_factors: Execution risk around significant new planned terminal openings.
A slower-than-expected recovery in the industrial economy, including tariff concerns.
Inability to extract strong price or yield improvements if the volume outlook softens or competitive price pressure arises.
A faster-than-forecast ramp in operating expenses or headcount that could hurt incremental margins as volumes recover.
A higher-than-historical-average valuation multiple could come under pressure from economic concerns or doubts about margin improvement.
